what.line: METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research, said 'meter'): a Berkeley nonprofit, founded by Beth Barnes, that measures how long a task an AI agent can finish on its own and tests frontier models for catastrophic autonomy risks

aka: ARC Evals (the team it grew from)

receipts.claim: paper 'Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks' (arXiv 2503.14499, 2025-03-18): the 50% time horizon of frontier AI doubled about every 7 months since 2019

Time Horizon 1.1 data file: doubling time 188 days over all years, 129 days (about 4.2 months) from 2023 on; GPT-2 (2019) 3 seconds, GPT-4 (2023) about 4 minutes, Claude Opus 4.6 (2026-02) about 12 hours

early Claude Mythos Preview (2026-04) scored a 50% horizon of about 17 hours (1,045 minutes), past the 16 hours METR calls the reliable ceiling of its task suite; the page says it is no longer actively updated
randomized trial (16 experienced open-source developers, 246 issues, Feb-Jun 2025): AI-allowed issues took 19% longer, while developers believed AI made them about 20% faster
says it has not accepted funding from AI companies, though it uses free tokens from them for evaluations

quotes.text: frontier AI time horizon has been doubling approximately every seven months since 2019

name_play.how: the lab is pronounced 'meter': a lyric about measuring can say its name without spelling it
a benchmark named like a sunset: the horizon line keeps moving away as you walk to it

readings: a taxi meter on an all-night ride

pivots.line: You felt faster. The clock said slower.

a y-axis labelled in human time: 1 minute, 1 hour, 1 workday, 1 week

what.line: OpenRouter: a single API and marketplace that routes developers' requests to hundreds of AI models, whose public token-share rankings show which models people actually pay to use

receipts.claim: raised US$113 million led by CapitalG at about a $1.3 billion valuation; 25 trillion tokens a week, up from 5 trillion six months earlier, across 400+ models (New York Times, syndicated)

with a16z published 'State of AI: An Empirical 100 Trillion Token Study': substantial open-weight adoption, outsized creative roleplay, the rise of agentic inference, and a 'Glass Slipper' effect in early user cohorts
raised $40 million seed and Series A (a16z, Menlo Ventures) in June 2025; CEO Alex Atallah co-founded OpenSea
weekly rankings in October 2026 were led by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, with Chinese open-weight models holding most of the top 10 by tokens
CAISI cited OpenRouter traffic as an adoption signal: DeepSeek V3.1 logged 97.5 million queries there in four weeks

what.line: Epoch AI: a research nonprofit that tracks the trends behind AI (training compute, data stocks, hardware, cost) and runs the FrontierMath benchmark

receipts.claim: training compute of notable models grew 4-5x per year from 2010 to May 2024 (frontier: about 5.3x)
estimated the stock of public human text at about 300 trillion effective tokens, likely exhausted by training runs between 2026 and 2032
OpenAI funded FrontierMath and had access to most problems except a holdout set; Epoch disclosed it only on 2024-12-20, the day o3 claimed about 25%
criticized in January 2025 for waiting to disclose the OpenAI funding; contributors said they had not been told

what.line: ARC Prize: the foundation and contest around ARC-AGI, François Chollet's puzzle benchmark of grids that humans find easy and AI finds hard, with a seven-figure prize for a system that matches people

OpenAI o3 scored 75.7% on the semi-private set within the compute limit and 87.5% at about 172x the compute

ARC Prize 2026 has over $2 million in prizes; final submission deadline 2026-11-02

what.line: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689): the first comprehensive AI law, sorting AI into four risk tiers from banned to unregulated, in force since 1 August 2024 and phased in through 2028

receipts.claim: entered into force 2024-08-01; prohibitions and AI literacy from 2025-02-02; general-purpose AI model duties from 2025-08-02
the AI Omnibus (proposed 2025-11-19, agreed 2026-05-07, in force 2026-07-27) pushed high-risk Annex III rules to 2027-12-02 and product-embedded systems to 2028-08-02
four risk levels: unacceptable (nine banned practices incl. social scoring), high, transparency (tell people they talk to a chatbot, label deepfakes), minimal
fines for banned practices up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
